name: Aminophylline

fields.mechanism_of_action: Aminophylline is a 2:1 complex of theophylline and ethylenediamine (aminophylline dihydrate is approximately 79% anhydrous theophylline by weight) and all of its pharmacological activity is attributable to the theophylline moiety. Theophylline is a methylxanthine with two distinct actions in the airways of patients with reversible obstruction: smooth muscle relaxation (bronchodilation) and suppression of the response of the airways to stimuli (non-bronchodilator prophylactic effects). While the mechanisms are not known with certainty, studies in animals suggest bronchodilation is mediated by inhibition of two isozymes of phosphodiesterase (PDE III and, to a lesser extent, PDE IV), while the non-bronchodilator prophylactic actions are probably mediated through one or more different molecular mechanisms that do not involve inhibition of PDE III or antagonism of adenosine receptors. Some adverse effects (hypotension, tachycardia, headache, emesis) appear to be mediated by inhibition of PDE III and by adenosine receptor antagonism. Theophylline also increases the force of contraction of diaphragmatic muscles (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, DESCRIPTION and CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Mechanism of Action).
indications: Intravenous aminophylline/theophylline: as an adjunct to inhaled beta-2 selective agonists and systemically administered corticosteroids for the treatment of acute exacerbations of the symptoms and reversible airflow obstruction associated with asthma and other chronic lung diseases, e.g. emphysema and chronic bronchitis (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE).

Oral theophylline (the moiety delivered by aminophylline; theophylline extended-release tablets): treatment of the symptoms and reversible airflow obstruction associated with chronic asthma and other chronic lung diseases, e.g. emphysema and chronic bronchitis (Theophylline extended-release tablet label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE).

Note on evidence: in most studies in patients treated for acute asthma exacerbations in an emergency department, addition of intravenous theophylline to inhaled beta-2 selective agonists and systemic corticosteroids did not produce greater bronchodilation and increased the risk of adverse effects; benefit has been shown in some hospitalized patients not responding adequately to inhaled beta-2 selective agonists. In COPD, theophylline decreases dyspnea, air trapping and the work of breathing and improves diaphragmatic contractility with little or no improvement in pulmonary function measurements (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Clinical Studies).
contraindications: Aminophylline is contraindicated in patients with a history of hypersensitivity to theophylline or other components in the product including ethylenediamine (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

Theophylline extended-release tablets are contraindicated in patients with a history of hypersensitivity to theophylline or other components in the product (Theophylline extended-release tablet label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).
side_effects: At peak serum theophylline concentrations below 20 mcg/mL, adverse reactions are generally mild and mainly consist of transient caffeine-like effects such as nausea, vomiting, headache and insomnia (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

At peak serum theophylline concentrations above 20 mcg/mL, theophylline produces a wide range of adverse reactions including persistent vomiting, cardiac arrhythmias and intractable seizures which can be lethal (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Other adverse reactions reported at serum theophylline concentrations below 20 mcg/mL include diarrhea, irritability, restlessness, fine skeletal muscle tremors and transient diuresis (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

In patients with hypoxia secondary to COPD, multifocal atrial tachycardia and flutter have been reported at serum theophylline concentrations of 15 mcg/mL or above (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Rare severe allergic skin reactions, including exfoliative dermatitis, after systemic administration in a patient previously sensitized by topical application of a substance containing ethylenediamine; patch tests are positive for ethylenediamine and negative for theophylline. Pharmacists and others with repeated skin exposure while handling aminophylline may develop contact dermatitis due to the ethylenediamine component (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Cardiac arrhythmias, including multifocal atrial tachycardia and ventricular arrhythmias, and intractable seizures are the characteristic life-threatening manifestations of theophylline toxicity (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS and OVERDOSAGE).

dosage.adult: Intravenous (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, Tables V and VI): loading dose, in a patient who has received no theophylline in the previous 24 hours, 4.6 mg/kg of theophylline (5.7 mg/kg as aminophylline) calculated on ideal body weight and administered over 30 minutes, which on average produces a maximum post-distribution serum concentration of 10 mcg/mL (range 6-16 mcg/mL). Constant intravenous infusion: in non-smoking adults initiate 0.4 mg/kg/hr of theophylline (0.5 mg/kg/hr as aminophylline) at the completion of the loading dose; the initial rate should not exceed 17 mg/hr (21 mg/hr as aminophylline) in patients with cor pulmonale, cardiac decompensation, liver dysfunction, or who are taking drugs that markedly reduce theophylline clearance (e.g. cimetidine) unless serum concentrations can be monitored at 24-hour intervals. Final dosage adjustment is guided by serum theophylline concentration: below 9.9 mcg/mL increase infusion rate about 25%; 10 to 14.9 mcg/mL maintain; 15 to 19.9 mcg/mL consider a 10% decrease; 20 to 24.9 mcg/mL decrease by 25%; 25 to 30 mcg/mL stop for 12 hours in children and 24 hours in adults and decrease the subsequent rate by at least 25%; above 30 mcg/mL stop the infusion and treat as overdose. Oral (theophylline extended-release tablet label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION): for chronic or long-term management and prevention of symptoms, not for acute symptoms of asthma or reversible bronchospasm; the dose must be individualised on peak serum theophylline concentration, and the dose required to reach a peak concentration of 10 to 20 mcg/mL varies fourfold between similar patients (approximately 400 mg/day to 1,600 mg/day in adults under 60 years).
dosage.geriatric: Elderly patients are at significantly greater risk of serious toxicity from theophylline than younger patients because of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic changes associated with ageing: clearance is reduced in patients over 60 years of age, protein binding may be decreased so that a larger proportion of the total serum concentration is in the pharmacologically active unbound form, and elderly patients appear more sensitive to the toxic effects of theophylline after chronic overdosage. The maximum infusion rate of theophylline in patients over 60 years should ordinarily not exceed 17 mg/hr (21 mg/hr as aminophylline) unless the patient remains symptomatic and the peak steady-state serum theophylline concentration is below 10 mcg/mL; rates above 17 mg/hr (21 mg/hr as aminophylline) should be prescribed with caution. For oral theophylline, the maximum daily dose in patients over 60 years should ordinarily not exceed 400 mg/day unless the patient continues to be symptomatic and the peak steady-state serum concentration is below 10 mcg/mL (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Geriatric Use and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION; Theophylline extended-release tablet label, PRECAUTIONS: Geriatric Use and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
dosage.paediatric: Theophylline is safe and effective for the approved indications in paediatric patients, but the maintenance dose must be selected with caution because the rate of theophylline clearance is highly variable across the paediatric age range, and due to the immaturity of theophylline metabolic pathways in patients under one year particular attention to dosage selection and frequent monitoring of serum theophylline concentrations is required. The constant infusion rate must be selected with caution in paediatric patients. Initial theophylline infusion rates after an appropriate loading dose (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Pediatric Use and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, Table V): neonates up to 24 days postnatal age 1 mg/kg every 12 hours; neonates beyond 24 days postnatal age 1.5 mg/kg every 12 hours (to target 7.5 mcg/mL for neonatal apnea); infants 6-52 weeks old, mg/kg/hr = (0.008 x age in weeks) + 0.21; young children 1-9 years 0.8 mg/kg/hr; older children 9-12 years 0.7 mg/kg/hr; adolescents 12-16 years who smoke cigarettes or marijuana 0.7 mg/kg/hr (not to exceed 900 mg/day unless serum levels indicate a larger dose is needed); adolescents 12-16 years who do not smoke 0.5 mg/kg/hr (not to exceed 400 mg/day unless serum levels indicate a larger dose is needed).

interactions: Drugs that decrease theophylline clearance (raise serum theophylline concentration), from the label's Table II: cimetidine (CYP1A2 inhibition, 70% increase); enoxacin (300% increase); ciprofloxacin (40% increase); allopurinol at doses of 600 mg/day or more (25% increase); disulfiram (50% increase); fluvoxamine; tacrine (90% increase); erythromycin (35% increase); clarithromycin (25% increase); troleandomycin (33-100% increase depending on dose); thiabendazole (190% increase); ticlopidine (60% increase); propranolol (100% increase); mexiletine (80% increase); interferon alpha-A (100% increase); estrogens (30% increase); pentoxifylline (30% increase); methotrexate (20% increase after low-dose MTX, higher doses may have a greater effect); propafenone (40% increase). Discontinuing a drug that increases theophylline clearance will result in accumulation to potentially toxic levels unless the theophylline dose is reduced (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions, Table II).

Drugs that increase theophylline clearance (lower serum theophylline concentration): rifampin (20-40% decrease); carbamazepine (30% decrease); phenobarbital (25% decrease after two weeks); phenytoin (serum theophylline and phenytoin concentrations decrease about 40%); aminoglutethimide (25% decrease); moricizine (25% decrease); sulfinpyrazone (20% decrease); isoproterenol IV (20% decrease). Discontinuation of a concomitant drug that inhibits theophylline clearance will result in decreased serum theophylline concentrations unless the theophylline dose is increased (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions, Table II).

Pharmacodynamic interactions: adenosine - theophylline blocks adenosine receptors, so higher doses of adenosine may be required; diazepam, flurazepam, lorazepam and midazolam - benzodiazepines increase CNS adenosine while theophylline blocks adenosine receptors, larger doses may be required, and discontinuation of theophylline without reducing the benzodiazepine dose may result in respiratory depression; ephedrine - synergistic CNS effects with increased nausea, nervousness and insomnia; halothane - increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias; ketamine - may lower the theophylline seizure threshold; lithium - theophylline increases renal lithium clearance and the lithium dose required to achieve a therapeutic serum concentration increased by an average of 60%; pancuronium - theophylline may antagonize nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockade; ethanol - a single large dose (3 mL/kg of whiskey) decreases theophylline clearance for up to 24 hours (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions, Table II).

Drugs documented not to interact with theophylline or producing no clinically significant interaction (<15% change in theophylline clearance) are listed in the label as: albuterol (systemic and inhaled), amoxicillin, ampicillin with or without sulbactam, atenolol, azithromycin, dietary caffeine, cefaclor, co-trimoxazole (trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole), diltiazem, dirithromycin, enflurane, famotidine, felodipine, finasteride, hydrocortisone, isoflurane, isoniazid, isradipine, influenza vaccine, ketoconazole, lomefloxacin, mebendazole, medroxyprogesterone, methylprednisolone, metronidazole, metoprolol, nadolol, nifedipine, nizatidine, norfloxacin, ofloxacin, omeprazole, prednisone and prednisolone, ranitidine, rifabutin, roxithromycin, sorbitol (purgative doses do not inhibit theophylline absorption), sucralfate, systemic terbutaline, terfenadine, tetracycline and tocainide (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions, Table III). The clinician should not assume a drug does not interact with theophylline if it is not listed in Table II, and the label notes that the tables were current as of 1 September 1995 and that new interactions are continuously being reported.

Other drugs that reduce theophylline clearance and require dose reduction and intensive serum monitoring: smoking cessation (cessation of smoking is listed as a cause of reduced theophylline clearance) (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS: Conditions That Reduce Theophylline Clearance).
fields.monitoring: Measure serum theophylline concentrations: before making a dose increase to determine whether the concentration is sub-therapeutic in a patient who continues to be symptomatic; whenever signs or symptoms of theophylline toxicity are present; and whenever there is a new illness, worsening of a concurrent illness or a change in the treatment regimen that may alter theophylline clearance (e.g. sustained fever of 102 degrees F or above for 24 hours or more, hepatitis, or addition/discontinuation of drugs listed in Table II). In patients who have received no theophylline in the previous 24 hours, measure a serum concentration 30 minutes after the intravenous loading dose, then a second measurement one expected half-life after starting the constant infusion (approximately 4 hours in children 1-9 years, 8 hours in non-smoking adults), and thereafter at 24-hour intervals for the duration of the infusion; serum concentrations may be measured at 24-hour intervals in acutely ill patients receiving intravenous theophylline. In patients in whom decreased serum protein binding is suspected (e.g. cirrhosis, women in the third trimester of pregnancy), measure unbound theophylline and adjust the dose to achieve an unbound concentration of 6-12 mcg/mL. Saliva concentrations cannot be used reliably to adjust dosage without special techniques. Theophylline at serum concentrations within the 10-20 mcg/mL range modestly increases plasma glucose, uric acid, free fatty acids, total cholesterol, HDL, the HDL/LDL ratio and urinary free cortisol excretion, and may transiently decrease serum triiodothyronine. If signs or symptoms of toxicity develop, stop the intravenous infusion and measure a serum theophylline concentration immediately (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Monitoring Serum Theophylline Concentrations and Effects on Laboratory Tests; WARNINGS).
fields.patient_counselling: Advise patients to withhold further doses and contact their clinician immediately if nausea or vomiting, particularly repetitive vomiting, or other signs of theophylline toxicity occur; the intravenous infusion should be stopped and a serum theophylline concentration measured immediately (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS: When Signs or Symptoms of Theophylline Toxicity Are Present). For oral theophylline, health care providers should instruct patients and caregivers to discontinue any dosage that causes adverse effects, withhold the medication until the symptoms are gone and then resume therapy at a lower, previously tolerated dosage, and not to take a dose that causes adverse effects (Theophylline extended-release tablet label, WARNINGS and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). Advise patients that theophylline and aminophylline are the same active chemical (aminophylline is the theophylline-ethylenediamine complex) and that all other medicines, including over-the-counter products, should be reported because many alter theophylline clearance. Advise patients not to start or stop smoking, as smoking increases theophylline clearance and cessation reduces it (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS: Conditions That Reduce Theophylline Clearance and PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions). Patients and caregivers should be alert for the emergence of symptoms of toxicity - persistent vomiting, tremor, restlessness, insomnia, tachycardia, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia and in severe cases seizures or arrhythmias - and should seek urgent care if these occur (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS and OVERDOSAGE).
warnings: Theophylline should be used with extreme caution in patients with active peptic ulcer disease, seizure disorders and cardiac arrhythmias (not including bradyarrhythmias), due to the increased risk of exacerbation of the concurrent condition (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS: Concurrent Illness).

There are several readily identifiable causes of reduced theophylline clearance; if the infusion rate is not appropriately reduced in the presence of these risk factors, severe and potentially fatal theophylline toxicity can occur. Risk factors: age (neonates term and premature, children under 1 year, elderly over 60 years); concurrent diseases (acute pulmonary edema, congestive heart failure, cor pulmonale, fever 102 degrees F or above for 24 hours or more or lesser elevations for longer periods, hypothyroidism, liver disease including cirrhosis and acute hepatitis, reduced renal function in infants under 3 months of age, sepsis with multi-organ failure, shock); cessation of smoking; and drug interactions (adding a drug that inhibits theophylline metabolism such as cimetidine, erythromycin or tacrine, or stopping a drug that enhances theophylline metabolism such as carbamazepine or rifampin) (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS: Conditions That Reduce Theophylline Clearance).

Other factors associated with decreased theophylline clearance include the third trimester of pregnancy, sepsis with multiple organ failure and hypothyroidism; careful attention to dose reduction and frequent monitoring of serum theophylline concentrations is required in these patients (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Miscellaneous).

Whenever a patient receiving theophylline develops nausea or vomiting, particularly repetitive vomiting, or other signs or symptoms consistent with theophylline toxicity, the intravenous infusion should be stopped and a serum theophylline concentration measured immediately (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS).

Increases in the dose of intravenous theophylline should not be made in response to an acute exacerbation of symptoms unless the steady-state serum theophylline concentration is below 10 mcg/mL, and infusion rate increases should generally be limited to about 25% of the previous infusion rate (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS: Dosage Increases).

For oral theophylline, increases in the dose should not be made in response to an acute exacerbation of symptoms of chronic lung disease, since theophylline provides little added benefit to inhaled beta-2 selective agonists and systemic corticosteroids in this circumstance and increases the risk of adverse effects; a peak steady-state serum theophylline concentration should be measured before increasing the dose for persistent chronic symptoms (Theophylline extended-release tablet label, WARNINGS: Dosage Increases).

Excessive doses of aminophylline are associated with severe toxicity: after a chronic overdosage, generalized seizures, life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias and death may occur at serum theophylline concentrations above 30 mcg/mL, and severity after chronic overdosage correlates more strongly with age than with the peak concentration, with patients over 60 years at greatest risk (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, OVERDOSAGE).

Theophylline must not be given concomitantly with monoamine oxidase inhibitors - hyperpyretic crises, severe convulsions and deaths have occurred in patients receiving tricyclic antidepressant and monoamine oxidase inhibiting drugs simultaneously (the equivalent warning for the class) - see the amitriptyline monograph; for theophylline itself the label's warnings are the clearance and toxicity warnings listed above (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS).

Theophylline extended-release tablets are recommended for chronic or long-term management and prevention of symptoms, and not for use in treating acute symptoms of asthma and reversible bronchospasm (Theophylline extended-release tablet label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
precautions: Careful consideration of the interacting drugs and physiologic conditions that can alter theophylline clearance and require dosage adjustment should occur prior to initiation of theophylline therapy, prior to increases in the theophylline dose and during follow-up (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: General; Theophylline extended-release tablet label, PRECAUTIONS: General).

The dose of theophylline must be individualized on the basis of serum theophylline concentration measurements in order to achieve maximum potential benefit with minimal risk of adverse effects; there is no single theophylline dose that will provide both safe and effective serum concentrations for all patients (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION; Theophylline extended-release tablet label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
Theophylline distributes poorly into body fat, therefore mg/kg doses should be calculated on the basis of ideal body weight (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

For the intravenous route, the constant infusion rate of theophylline must be selected with caution in pediatric patients since the rate of theophylline clearance is highly variable across the age range from neonates to adolescents (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Pediatric Use).

In vitro and in vivo studies: long-term carcinogenicity studies in mice and rats have been carried out; theophylline was not shown to be genotoxic in Ames Salmonella, cytogenetics, micronucleus and Chinese hamster ovary test systems. In a 14-week continuous breeding study theophylline impaired fertility in mice at oral doses of 120, 270 and 500 mg/kg, and in 13-week toxicity studies systemic toxicity including decreased testicular weight was observed in rats and mice at 40-300 mg/kg (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, and Impairment of Fertility).

Most serum theophylline assays in clinical use are immunoassays specific for theophylline; other xanthines such as caffeine, dyphylline and pentoxifylline are not detected by these assays, but some drugs (e.g. cefazolin, cephalothin) may interfere with certain HPLC techniques (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: The Effect of Other Drugs on Theophylline Serum Concentration Measurements).

Theophylline is only weakly dialysed and is not effectively removed by peritoneal dialysis; in overdose, charcoal haemoperfusion is the most effective extracorporeal method, increasing clearance up to six-fold but with serious complications including hypotension, hypocalcemia, platelet consumption and bleeding diatheses (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, OVERDOSAGE: Extracorporeal Removal).
serious_adverse_reactions: Intractable seizures (often resistant to anticonvulsant therapy, potentially causing irreversible brain injury) and death (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS and OVERDOSAGE).

Life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, including multifocal atrial tachycardia and atrial flutter, ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS and OVERDOSAGE).
Persistent vomiting and intractable seizures with cardiovascular collapse at serum theophylline concentrations above 20 mcg/mL (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Hypokalemia (85% and 79% of patients in two studies of theophylline toxicity with serum concentrations above 30 mcg/mL), hyperglycemia (98% in acute overdose), and acid-base disturbance (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS, Table IV).

Death from theophylline toxicity is most often secondary to cardiorespiratory arrest and/or hypoxic encephalopathy following prolonged generalized seizures or intractable cardiac arrhythmias causing hemodynamic compromise (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, OVERDOSAGE).
Severe allergic skin reactions including exfoliative dermatitis in patients previously sensitised to ethylenediamine (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
food_interactions: Taking theophylline extended-release tablets immediately after a high-fat content meal may result in a somewhat higher Cmax, a delayed Tmax and a somewhat greater extent of absorption; however, the differences are usually not great and the product may normally be administered without regard to meals (Theophylline extended-release tablet label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

Dietary caffeine does not interact with theophylline; caffeine is listed among the drugs documented not to interact with theophylline (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions, Table III).
The Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label does not describe a food interaction for the intravenous route.
fields.pregnancy_guidance: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women and no teratogenicity studies in nonrodents. Theophylline was not shown to be teratogenic in CD-1 mice at oral doses up to 400 mg/kg (about 2.0 times the maximum recommended human dose on a mg/m2 basis) or in CD-1 rats at oral doses up to 260 mg/kg (about 3.0 times the recommended human dose on a mg/m2 basis); at 220 mg/kg embryotoxicity was observed in rats in the absence of maternal toxicity. Reduced theophylline clearance in the third trimester of pregnancy requires careful attention to dose reduction and frequent monitoring of serum theophylline concentrations. Theophylline should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Pregnancy and WARNINGS; Theophylline extended-release tablet label, PRECAUTIONS: Pregnancy).
fields.lactation_guidance: Theophylline is excreted into breast milk and may cause irritability or other signs of mild toxicity in nursing human infants; the concentration of theophylline in breast milk is about equivalent to the maternal serum concentration, and an infant ingesting a litre of breast milk containing 10-20 mcg/mL of theophylline per day is likely to receive 10-20 mg of theophylline per day. Serious adverse effects in the infant are unlikely unless the mother has toxic serum theophylline concentrations (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, PRECAUTIONS: Nursing Mothers; Theophylline extended-release tablet label, PRECAUTIONS: Nursing Mothers).
fields.overdose: Management of theophylline overdose: stop the theophylline infusion; contact a regional poison centre; institute supportive care including intravenous access, airway maintenance and electrocardiographic monitoring; treat seizures rapidly and aggressively with an intravenous benzodiazepine (e.g. diazepam 0.1-0.2 mg/kg every 1-3 minutes until seizures are terminated) and treat repetitive seizures with phenobarbital 20 mg/kg infused over 30-60 minutes (phenytoin is ineffective); anticipate and consider prophylactic anticonvulsant therapy in high-risk patients (acute overdose with serum concentrations above 100 mcg/mL, or chronic overdosage in patients over 60 years with concentrations above 30 mcg/mL); treat cardiac arrhythmias other than sinus tachycardia and simple ventricular premature beats with antiarrhythmic therapy appropriate to the arrhythmia; measure serum theophylline immediately on presentation, then 2-4 hours later and at intervals of about every 4 hours; and enhance clearance with multiple-dose oral activated charcoal (0.5 mg/kg up to 20 g every two hours) or extracorporeal removal. Charcoal haemoperfusion is the most effective extracorporeal method (increasing clearance up to six-fold) but serious complications may occur; haemodialysis is about as efficient as multiple-dose oral charcoal with a lower risk of serious complications, serum concentrations may rebound 5-10 mcg/mL after discontinuing charcoal haemoperfusion or haemodialysis, and peritoneal dialysis is ineffective (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, OVERDOSAGE).
fields.pharmacokinetics: The pharmacokinetics of theophylline vary widely among similar patients and cannot be predicted by age, sex, body weight or other demographic characteristics; concurrent illnesses, alterations in normal physiology and co-administration of other drugs significantly alter them, and within-subject variability in metabolism has been reported, especially in acutely ill patients. Mean total body clearance and half-life (Hospira label, Table I): otherwise healthy non-smoking adults aged 16-60 years 0.65 mL/kg/min (range 0.27-1.03) with a half-life of 8.7 hours (range 6.1-12.8); elderly non-smokers over 60 years 0.41 mL/kg/min (0.21-0.61) with a half-life of 9.8 hours (1.6-18); children 1-4 years 1.7 mL/kg/min with a half-life of 3.4 hours; premature neonates 0.29-0.64 mL/kg/min with half-lives of 30 and 20 hours. Clearance is reduced by acute pulmonary edema, COPD with cor pulmonale, cirrhosis (0.31 mL/kg/min, half-life 32 hours), acute hepatitis, cholestasis, hypothyroidism (0.38 mL/kg/min), sepsis with multi-organ failure, the third trimester of pregnancy and by smoking cessation, and is increased by hyperthyroidism (0.8 mL/kg/min), cystic fibrosis (1.25 mL/kg/min), low carbohydrate/high protein diets, parenteral nutrition and daily consumption of charcoal-broiled beef. About 40% of theophylline is bound to plasma protein, primarily albumin, and the apparent volume of distribution is approximately 0.45 L/kg (range 0.3-0.7 L/kg) based on ideal body weight; theophylline passes freely across the placenta, into breast milk and into cerebrospinal fluid. In adults and children beyond one year of age approximately 90% of the dose is metabolised in the liver by demethylation to 1-methylxanthine and 3-methylxanthine and by hydroxylation to 1,3-dimethyluric acid, with cytochrome P450 1A2 catalysing demethylation to 3-methylxanthine and cytochromes P450 2E1 and P450 3A3 catalysing hydroxylation; about 6% of a theophylline dose is N-methylated to caffeine. Both biotransformation pathways are capacity-limited, so nonlinearity of elimination may begin in some patients at serum theophylline concentrations below 10 mcg/mL and dose changes should be made in small increments (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Pharmacokinetics, Table I, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion and Miscellaneous).
clinical_pearls: Aminophylline is not a separate active drug: it is the 2:1 theophylline-ethylenediamine complex (aminophylline dihydrate is about 79% anhydrous theophylline by weight), and 25 mg/mL of aminophylline equals 19.7 mg/mL of anhydrous theophylline; all dosing is effectively theophylline dosing, and aminophylline = theophylline / 0.8 (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, DESCRIPTION and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, Table V).

Therapeutic window: bronchodilation occurs over serum theophylline concentrations of 5-20 mcg/mL, clinically important improvement in symptom control and pulmonary function generally requires concentrations above 10 mcg/mL, and maintaining an average concentration of 10-15 mcg/mL achieves most of the therapeutic benefit while minimising serious adverse events (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Serum Concentration-Effect Relationship).

Ethylenediamine is a second allergen: severe exfoliative dermatitis can occur in patients previously sensitised to ethylenediamine, and pharmacists handling aminophylline repeatedly may develop contact dermatitis (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Smoking status must be reviewed before dosing: smoking increases theophylline clearance and, critically, smoking cessation reduces clearance and can precipitate toxicity if the dose is not reduced (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS: Conditions That Reduce Theophylline Clearance).

Serum concentrations, not dose, drive dosing: because the dose required to achieve 10-20 mcg/mL varies fourfold between otherwise similar patients, all dose changes should be guided by serum levels, and dose increases limited to about 25% of the previous infusion rate (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, WARNINGS and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, Table VI).

Acute theophylline overdose is usually more forgiving than chronic overdosage: acute overdose patients are less likely to seize unless the peak concentration exceeds 100 mcg/mL, whereas after chronic overdosage seizures, life-threatening arrhythmias and death occur above 30 mcg/mL, with severity correlating more strongly with age than with concentration (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, OVERDOSAGE).

Intravenous aminophylline has a limited role in acute asthma: most emergency department studies show no greater bronchodilation and increased adverse effects when it is added to inhaled beta-2 agonists and systemic corticosteroids (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Clinical Studies).

Oral aminophylline products are not approved in the United States; the oral theophylline moiety is supplied as theophylline extended-release tablets, which are for chronic management and prevention, not for acute bronchospasm (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label; Theophylline extended-release tablet label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No renal dose adjustment is necessary in adults and children over 3 months of age: the label states that since little theophylline is excreted unchanged in the urine and since active metabolites of theophylline do not accumulate to clinically significant levels even in the face of end-stage renal disease, no dosage adjustment for renal insufficiency is necessary. In neonates approximately 50% of the theophylline dose is excreted unchanged in the urine, so careful attention to dose reduction and frequent monitoring of serum theophylline concentrations is required in neonates with reduced renal function, and reduced renal function in infants under 3 months of age is listed as a risk factor for reduced theophylline clearance (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Excretion and WARNINGS: Conditions That Reduce Theophylline Clearance).
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is specified. Liver disease (cirrhosis, acute hepatitis, cholestasis) reduces theophylline clearance - mean clearance 0.31-0.35 mL/kg/min with half-lives of 19-32 hours - and requires dose reduction and intensive serum monitoring; in patients with liver dysfunction the initial theophylline infusion rate should not exceed 17 mg/hr (21 mg/hr as aminophylline) unless serum concentrations can be monitored at 24-hour intervals, and 5 days may be required before steady state is reached (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY: Table I and Miscellaneous, WARNINGS: Conditions That Reduce Theophylline Clearance, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: General Considerations).
fields.administration_instructions: Intravenous: administer by slow intravenous injection or diluted and administered by intravenous infusion (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, DESCRIPTION). Aminophylline injection should not be mixed in a syringe with other drugs but should be added separately to the intravenous solution; when given 'piggyback', the intravenous system already in place should be turned off while the aminophylline is infused if there is a potential problem with admixture incompatibility. Because of the alkalinity of aminophylline-containing solutions, drugs known to be alkali labile should be avoided in admixtures, including epinephrine HCl, norepinephrine bitartrate, isoproterenol HCl and penicillin G potassium. Inspect parenteral products visually for particulate matter and discoloration before administration; do not administer unless the solution is clear and the container is undamaged; discard the unused portion; do not use if crystals have separated from the solution (Hospira Aminophylline Injection, USP label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: Intravenous Admixture Incompatibility and HOW SUPPLIED). Oral: theophylline extended-release tablets may normally be administered without regard to meals, although taking them immediately after a high-fat meal may result in a somewhat higher Cmax and delayed Tmax (Theophylline extended-release tablet label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

notes: The table stores this agent as 'Aminophylline'. Aminophylline is the INN/BAN name for the 2:1 theophylline-ethylenediamine complex (aminophylline dihydrate is approximately 79% anhydrous theophylline by weight); the pharmacological activity, dosing, interactions and toxicity all belong to the theophylline moiety. In the United States the only approved product is the generic intravenous aminophylline injection (Hospira) - there is no FDA-approved oral aminophylline product - so the oral theophylline extended-release tablet label (Amneal) is used as the authoritative source for oral theophylline dosing and the oral formulation information, and this is stated explicitly where used. No branded aminophylline product is listed on DailyMed, so brand_names is empty. Note also that the Hospira label's drug-interaction tables carry a September 1995 currency date and the label explicitly warns that new interactions with new chemical entities are continuously being reported, so the table should be read alongside current product labels. This is a drug-specific monograph rather than a shared template: the point that aminophylline equals theophylline/0.8 is stated explicitly, but the clearance, interaction and toxicity content is specific to aminophylline/theophylline as labelled.
